hints: If you were told you must sell on day i, which buying day would you pick? Can you know that answer without looking back over all earlier days?
Single pass over prices while remembering the cheapest price seen so far. Each day, the best sale today is price − minSoFar; keep the maximum of that.

1. minPrice = prices[0], best = 0.
  2. For each day: best = max(best, prices[i] − minPrice).
  3. Then minPrice = min(minPrice, prices[i]).
  4. Return best.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.idea: Try every buy day i and every later sell day j and keep the best difference.

approaches.name: Optimal
approaches.idea: Track the minimum price so far; selling today earns price − min, so one pass finds the best.

explain: For prices = [7, 1, 5, 3, 6, 4]: the minimum becomes 1 on day 1; selling at 5 earns 4, at 3 earns 2, at 6 earns 5 (the best), at 4 earns 3, so the function returns 5. Updating the profit before the minimum makes sure the buy day is never after the sell day. If prices only fall, as in [9, 7, 4, 1], every difference is ≤ 0, so best stays 0. A single day also gives 0.
recognize: "Buy once, sell later, maximise profit" → running minimum and best difference in one pass.
